_about: Is this the name of a thing, or the title of a page?
Every 'page' case is a title that reached the candidate list in a real
session log under runtime/ -- most of them were *selected* and said
out loud as a recommendation. Every 'thing' case is a real product,
place or creative work, and the creative works are the reason this
file exists in two halves: a film or a drama is named with a sentence
often enough ('Don't Look Up', 'Get Out', 'Watch Dogs') that a rule
strict enough to catch every headline would throw them away.
So some pages are deliberately NOT here. 'Realize Cooking Doesn't
Really Burn Off' is a headline, and it is shaped exactly like a film
title; the name cannot decide it. What decides it is that the person
asked how to make something, which has no candidates at all -- and
that is tested where it is decided, in test_candidate_titles.py.
expect  page  = must not be a candidate
shape   the kind of thing the recommendation expected: product,
place, or any (unknown -- which is where films and dramas are)
